title: Composition of the book of Daniel (date and authorship debated)
summary: The book presents stories about Daniel in the third person (chs. 1–6) and visions in his own first person (chs. 7–12), and says he wrote down his dream (7:1) and was told to seal the book (12:4). When and by whom it was composed is disputed: traditionally in the sixth century BC by Daniel; on the widespread critical view, in its final form in Judaea during Antiochus IV's persecution (c. 167–164 BC), with the stories perhaps earlier.
external_reason: Book-level historical question required by SPEC 5.5 and Milestone 5 ("composition dating debates"); modelled as an event so that its evidence, competing positions and review status are published like other research.
